title: Micro-reflect and risk catalog for ongoing PRs
content:
Context:
Notes-to-self after cycling through four PRs this sprint (mostly small-batch performance fixes + one refactor that touched kv-cache eviction). Goal: capture quick heuristics, risk catalog, follow-ups that I can turn into tickets later. Keep this concise — use as a checklist before marking a PR ready for merge or for post-merge follow-up.

1) Quick mental checklist (fast pass, ~3–5 min)
- Does the PR change any public contract (API / config defaults / behavior that other services rely on)? If yes -> add 'compatibility' label and notify owners.
- Are there new long-running goroutines/background loops or added timers? Check shutdown semantics.
- DB / state mutations: are they idempotent and retriable? Add a simple unit test for the happy and failure path.
- Surface area: does the change span more than two subsystems (serving, routing, tracing)? If yes -> flag as cross-team.
- CI footprint: do unit/integration tests pass locally (quick run) and does CI create any flakiness? If flaky, note patterns (timeout, auth, env).

2) Risk scoring rubric I used (subjective but consistent)
- R1 (Low): small docstrings, variable renames, pure cosmetic. No prod impact.
- R2 (Low-Med): refactors limited to one module with existing tests.
- R3 (Medium): touches runtime hot path but only adds checks/metrics; small perf risk.
- R4 (High): changes batching/kv-cache/query path; potential to alter latency/cost profiles.
- R5 (Critical): modifies routing/fallbacks or rolling upgrade behavior; requires rollout plan and canary.

Example: the eviction change in PR #1427 I reviewed felt R4 — altered hit-rate and eviction order in tight loops.

3) Concrete follow-ups to create tickets for (title suggestions + short acceptance criteria)
- "INF: kv-cache eviction telemetry to gauge regressions" — Add histograms for eviction rate, miss/hit by prefix, and a dashboard. AC: dashboard shows baseline + 90th/99th by model and shows eviction counts in last 24h.
- "perf: isolate hotpath allocation in tokenizer for small requests" — Add microbench and compare allocations before/after. AC: <10% alloc reduction for 32-token requests.
- "safety: add canary/rollback notes for routing policy changes" — document fallback behavior and add a smoke test that intentionally exhausts capacity. AC: documented steps + test in the canary job.

4) Refactor/cleanup ideas (tiny diffs I sketched while reading code)
- serving/runtime/streamer.go: split sendLoop into two funcs (prepareTokens + emit) to narrow scope for future error handling. Diff likely < 40 LOC and safe.
- platform/metrics/collector: unify label names (model -> model_name) in one pass; add compatibility shim for old dashboards. Plan: one PR that replaces uses and a follow-up to delete shim.
- routing/policy: move policy evaluation into a pure function so it can be tested deterministically (avoid reading global config during evaluation).

5) Quick grep & local commands I ran (notes so I can repeat)
- git checkout -b tmp/rvw-evict && git fetch origin && git pull origin/main
- git --no-pager grep -n "evict" -- serving | sed -n '1,80p'  # find hotspots
- go test ./... -run TestKVCacheEvict -v  # local targeted test
- bench: go test ./bench -run BenchmarkTokenize -bench=. -benchmem

6) Suggested reviewers and why
- Lina Park — wrote original kv-cache patch and good at correctness proofs.
- Theo Alvarez — perf measurements and microbench experience.
- Mina R. (if available) — infra tolerability/rollout experience.

7) Unresolved questions to call out in PR description (include command to reproduce)
- Do we need to preserve strict LRU semantics for small models? (I couldn't find a test asserting canonical ordering.)
- Is the eviction signal currently emitted under a global lock? If so, does that block live inference during bursts? Repro: stress-test script in /tools/loaders/stress_kv.sh (args: --qps 200 --payload small).

8) Post-merge quick checks (run within 30–60m after merge)
- Monitor dashboard: 50th/95th latency, eviction rate, error-rate for affected routes.
- Quick smoke: curl /health endpoint from two AZs and ensure model serve responds.
- Rollback plan: confirm that the revert PR is ready (template filled) and estimated rollback time < 15 minutes.

9) TODO & ticket draft lines (copy-paste into Jira)
- [ ] Create INF-2123: "kv-cache eviction telemetry to gauge regressions" -> assign to Lina, estimate 1 spike day + 1/2 day dashboard follow-up.
- [ ] Create PERF-331: "tokenizer alloc microbench" -> assign to Theo, include before/after numbers.
- [ ] Create OPS-78: "canary script for routing fallback" -> owner: SRE on-call.

10) Final personal notes (bits of rationale)
- When in doubt, prefer a small canary with a narrow user slice vs a global roll. The cost of a revert is often underestimated.
- Small refactors that improve testability pay dividends; if I can separate pure logic from side-effects in 20 LOC, do it in the PR.
- Use the rubric above to move conversations off-the-line (e.g., "this is R3, we should run canary") — helps with async decision-making.

---
Raw scratch area (dumped commands / small logs):
[2026-03-08 10:12] local bench before: allocations/op=784 mem=45KB
[2026-03-08 12:03] after small change to tokenizer: allocations/op=623 mem=38KB (rough)
PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1427  -> left inline comments about metrics and one todo to add a shim.

Notes to self: convert this doc into 3 Jira tickets tomorrow morning, add dashboard link in INF-2123, and ping Lina in Slack for a short pairing session on eviction semantics.
